title: LangChain-AI/deepagents: agent harness
content:
Deep Agents is an open source agent harness — an opinionated agent that runs out of the box. Extend, override, or replace any piece.
Principles:
- Opinionated — defaults tuned for long-horizon, multi-step work
- Extensible — override or replace any piece without forking
- Model-agnostic — works with any LLM that supports tool calling: frontier, open-weight, or local
- Production-ready — built on LangGraph (streaming, persistence, checkpointing) with first-class tracing, evaluation, and deployment via LangSmith
Features include:
- Sub-agents — delegate tasks to agents with isolated context windows
- Filesystem — read, write, edit, or search over pluggable local, sandboxed, or remote backends
- Context management — summarize long threads and offload tool outputs to disk
- Shell access — run commands in your sandbox of choice
- Persistent memory — pluggable state and store backends for cross-session recall
- Human-in-the-loop — approve, edit, or reject tool calls before they run
- Skills — reusable behaviors the agent can load on demand
- Tools — bring your own functions or any MCP server
Deep Agents is available as a JavaScript/TypeScript library — see deepagents.js.
Note
Deep Agents Code — a pre-built coding agent in your terminal, similar to Claude Code or Cursor, powered by any LLM. Install with curl -LsSf https://langch.in/dcode | bash. See the documentation for the full feature set.
uv add deepagentsfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent
agent = create_deep_agent(
    model="openai:gpt-5.5",
    tools=[my_custom_tool],
    system_prompt="You are a research assistant.",
)
result = agent.invoke({"messages": "Research LangGraph and write a summary"})
The agent can plan, read/write files, and manage its own context. Add your own tools, swap models, customize prompts, configure sub-agents, and more. See the documentation for full details.
Tip
For developing, debugging, and deploying AI agents and LLM applications, see LangSmith.
LangGraph is the graph runtime. LangChain's create_agent is a minimal agent harness on top of it. Deep Agents is a more opinionated harness on top of create_agent — same building blocks, but with filesystem, sub-agents, context management, and skills bundled in. For how the three relate, see the LangChain ecosystem overview.
Yes. Any model that supports tool calling works — frontier APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), open-weight models hosted on providers like Baseten or Fireworks, and self-hosted models via Ollama, vLLM, or llama.cpp. Use any LangChain chat model.
Yes! Deep Agents is built on LangGraph, designed for production agent deployments. Pair it with LangSmith for tracing, evaluation, and monitoring. See Going to production for the full guide.
All three are layers in the same stack — see the LangChain ecosystem overview for how they relate. Use Deep Agents when you want the full harness — planning, context management, delegation — out of the box. Use LangChain's create_agent when you want a lighter harness without the bundled middleware. Drop to LangGraph when the agent loop itself isn't the right shape and you need a custom graph.
The layers compose: any LangGraph CompiledStateGraph can be passed in as a sub-agent to a Deep Agent, so custom orchestration plugs in alongside the harness's defaults.

- LangChain ecosystem overview — how Deep Agents, LangChain, LangGraph, and LangSmith fit together
- API reference — complete reference for all public classes, functions, and types
- Discussions — community forum for technical questions, ideas, and feedback
- LangChain Academy — Comprehensive, free courses on LangChain libraries and products, made by the LangChain team.
- Contributing Guide — how to contribute and find good first issues

Inspired by Claude Code: an attempt to identify what makes it general-purpose, and push that further.
Deep Agents follows a "trust the LLM" model. The agent can do anything its tools allow. Enforce boundaries at the tool/sandbox level, not by expecting the model to self-police. See the security policy for more information.

report.summary: LangChain releases Deep Agents, an open-source, extensible agent harness for production-grade, long-horizon AI tasks across any tool-calling model.
report.background: Deep Agents emerges from LangChain's ecosystem as a more opinionated successor to their minimal create_agent harness, built on LangGraph. It is inspired by Claude Code, aiming to generalize that coding agent's capabilities into a reusable framework for arbitrary long-horizon, multi-step work. The rise of agentic AI has exposed a gap between simple prompt loops and reliable production systems; Deep Agents addresses this by bundling defaults for sub-agent delegation, filesystem access, context management, shell use, persistent memory, and human-in-the-loop approval. It remains model-agnostic, supporting frontier APIs, open-weight models, and local runtimes like Ollama, vLLM, and llama.cpp. The project is available as a Python library and a JavaScript/TypeScript port, with a pre-built terminal coding agent (Deep Agents Code) also provided.
key_points: Opinionated but extensible: Deep Agents ships with tuned defaults for complex, long-running tasks, yet every component can be overridden or replaced without forking the repository. This balance gives teams both immediate usability and full customization control, letting them adapt the agent to specific workflows.

Model-agnostic by design: It works with any LLM supporting tool calls, including GPT-5.5, Claude, Gemini, open-weight models on Baseten/Fireworks, and self-hosted options. This avoids vendor lock-in and allows switching models without rewriting the agent logic.

Production features built in: Leveraging LangGraph, it includes streaming, persistence, checkpointing, and first-class integration with LangSmith for tracing and evaluation. This makes it suitable for deployment rather than just prototyping, addressing a major challenge in agentic AI reliability.

Sub-agent architecture: The harness can delegate tasks to agents with isolated context windows, preventing context bloat and enabling parallel or specialized work. Custom LangGraph graphs can also be plugged in as sub-agents, making orchestration composable.

Security model: Deep Agents adopts a 'trust the LLM' approach, enabling agents to use all available tools while enforcing boundaries at the tool or sandbox level. This clarifies responsibility: developers must secure tool access rather than rely on model self-policing.
report.impact: For AI developers, Deep Agents reduces the effort to build production-grade agents by providing a coherent middleware layer—filesystem, context management, memory, and human oversight—out of the box. It likely accelerates adoption of agentic patterns in enterprise settings where observability and deployment matter. For the industry, it strengthens LangChain's position as the default orchestration stack, especially as teams seek model-agnostic solutions amid model fragmentation. Regular users would notice downstream applications becoming more capable of handling complex, multi-step requests—like research, coding, and data analysis—with transparent checkpoints and safer tool execution. The sub-agent and context-management features also mitigate common failures like lost context and poor long-horizon planning, leading to more reliable AI assistants.
report.tools: Try Deep Agents by installing via `uv add deepagents` or the JS/TS library. For a terminal coding agent, run the installation script from langch.in/dcode. Pair it with LangSmith for tracing and evaluation, and explore LangGraph for custom orchestration. For local model testing, use Ollama, vLLM, or llama.cpp with any tool-calling model.
